news.title: ChatGPT Reaches 20% of Google’s Search Volume
news.description: According to Adam Fry of OpenAI, ChatGPT now handles approximately one-fifth of the number of search-like queries handled by Google. ChatGPT would therefore be ahead of Bing, which holds about 5% of the search market.

news.title: Netflix Tests an AI-Powered Discover Tab to Recommend Content
news.description: Netflix’s new Discover tab uses artificial intelligence to help users find a program based on their mood.

news.title: Apple Opens Siri’s AI to All Apps
news.description: Apple now allows app developers to integrate their content and actions with Siri through a developer preview. Integrations could include checking a delivery, booking a service, or combining multiple actions.

news.title: Google Threatens to Cut Off Search for Schools That Ban AI
news.description: Google plans to remove Search access from student accounts managed by schools that reject its AI tools. Beginning in early 2027, institutions will also have to manually enable several AI features that are disabled by default.

news.title: Anthropic Is Working on a System to Prove AI Model Identity
news.description: Anthropic is developing a system intended to prove the identity of artificial intelligence models.

news.title: Canva Cuts Jobs, Affecting 22% of Its Workforce
news.description: Canva’s first layoffs affect 22% of its staff, in what the company describes as its most difficult moment.

news.title: SpaceX Chooses Qualcomm to Build Starlink’s 5G Network
news.description: SpaceX has hired Qualcomm to build a terrestrial 5G network for Starlink Mobile, with base stations to be deployed in the United States starting in 2027. The agreement covers tens of thousands of sites using Qualcomm’s Dragonwing platform.

news.title: Revolut Cuts AI Coding Costs Tenfold by Dropping Claude
news.description: UK fintech Revolut is reducing its AI-related coding costs by eliminating Claude and hosting its models itself.

news.title: Valve Changes Steam Publishing Rules Amid Influx of AI Games
news.description: Valve has changed its Steam publishing rules as the platform faces an influx of games using artificial intelligence.

news.title: Data Centers Turn to Former Jet Engines to Generate Power
news.description: Data centers are using former jet engines as power-access wait times grow longer.

news.title: Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in a $6.3 Billion Heist
news.description: Hackers used fake job interviews to organize a $6.3 billion theft targeting Binance.

news.title: Meta Seeks to Raise Up to $25 Billion in Debt to Fund AI
news.description: Meta is seeking to raise up to $25 billion in the debt markets as its artificial intelligence spending increases.

news.title: Advice for a Tesla Model 3 Battery Nearing the End of Its Warranty
news.description: A Tesla Model 3’s long-range battery is reaching the end of its eight-year warranty. The owner asks whether they should keep driving it as is or take any specific measures.

news.title: Buying a Used Tesla Model Y from an Independent Dealer
news.description: A buyer is looking for a 2022 or 2023 Model Y Long Range AWD, with a clean title and between 30,000 and 40,000 miles. They are asking for advice from people who bought their Tesla from a third-party dealer.

news.title: Climate Control Error on a 2019 Tesla Model 3 Performance
news.description: An owner reports the “VCFRONT_a160_compressorInhibited” and “lowSuctionPressure” errors. One response distinguishes a transient error, which may disappear when conditions change, from a genuine problem, particularly one caused by insufficient refrigerant.

news.title: Suspected Cyberattacks Destroy Food in European Supermarkets
news.description: More than 40 supermarkets across seven countries were affected by suspected attacks that remotely raised the temperature of refrigeration systems, destroying food. The incidents highlight the exposure of connected operational equipment whose software may no longer be supported.

news.title: OpenAI Plans to Merge Chat and Work Spaces in ChatGPT
news.description: OpenAI is preparing to merge Chat and Work tabs in ChatGPT within a single platform, while Codex would remain separate with a shared usage quota. The company has also added voice chat to its personal finance tool, and an enigmatic message hints at a new model.

news.title: Tesla and SpaceX Fall More Than 4% Before the Open
news.description: Tesla and SpaceX shares fell more than 4% in premarket trading after the election results.

news.title: Companies Assess Democratic Impact on AI and Data Centers
news.description: Business and tech leaders are already assessing what Democratic control could change for artificial intelligence, data centers, and their access to Washington.

news.title: Claude Code Executive Leaves Anthropic Before Its IPO
news.description: Cat Wu, who helped turn Claude Code from a prototype into a successful product, left Anthropic a few weeks before its expected IPO. She did not specify the reasons for her departure.

news.title: Spy Recorder Discovered in an OpenAI Conference Room
news.description: Security personnel from the U.S. Department of Justice discovered an audio recorder hidden behind a television in an OpenAI conference room. The company says it identified the responsible employee using its own AI models; the employee was fired and indicted.

news.title: Claude Reaches One-Fifth of Google’s Search Volume
news.description: OpenAI claims that ChatGPT handles approximately one-fifth of Google’s search-type queries. The number of weekly users reportedly rose from 1 to 1.2 billion in about 60 days.

news.title: Anthropic Says Claude Speeds Up Custom Chip Design
news.description: Anthropic told investors before its IPO that Claude was helping its 15-person chip team design custom silicon more quickly. The claim is based on its own estimates.

news.title: AI Agents Operate a SETI Telescope
news.description: The SETI Institute and Breakthrough Listen are using AI agents to operate the Allen Telescope Array and analyze radio signals live. Tasks that previously took several weeks are completed in a few hours, with a first real-time detection of a known pulsar.

news.title: A Codex Setting Could Allow Training on Your Conversations
news.description: A user claims that the “Improve the model for everyone” option was re-enabled on their account, which could allow OpenAI to use their Codex conversations to train its models. The report is unconfirmed, but the option and the “Include environments” setting can be checked separately.

news.title: GPT-6 Astra Reportedly Designed a Complete Device in Less Than a Week
news.description: OpenAI’s hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device intended for Codex, from the casing to the embedded software and printed circuit board. Several corrections were needed, partly because the model did not always account for manufacturing tolerances.

news.title: OpenAI Introduces LifeVal, an AI Test for Everyday Tasks
news.description: LifeVal measures an AI’s ability to make appointments, shop for groceries, or fill out administrative forms. The test’s areas are based in part on a survey of 4,000 people and have been used internally by OpenAI for a year.

news.title: OpenAI May Be Wary of Jensen Huang’s Influence
news.description: Silicon Valley figures are concerned about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s financial and political power, as well as his control over access to AI chips. OpenAI is reportedly avoiding taking a public position on chip sales to China to avoid upsetting its supplier.

news.title: Uber President Joins OpenAI to Lead Communications
news.description: Jill Hazelbaker, who previously worked at Google and Snap, will lead OpenAI’s global communications and brand strategy. She will be tasked with stabilizing a team marked by several executive departures ahead of a possible IPO.

news.title: Fal Doubles Its Valuation in Seven Months on Generative AI Demand
news.description: Fal’s valuation rose from $8 billion to $16 billion since April, following a $1.3 billion funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners. Its annualized revenue exceeded $800 million, despite low margins caused by the cost of computing.

news.title: Democratic Wave Pushes Back Against Tech Right
news.description: The Democratic victories recorded on election night were fueled by opposition to data centers. They also represented a rejection of Silicon Valley elites and their vision of the future.

news.title: An AI Website Model with Dual Interfaces for Humans and Agents
news.description: A new study conducted with Knotch proposes websites with two surfaces: an intent-responsive interface for humans and a service-oriented semantic interface for agents. Both would rely on a shared brand context model capable of keeping the company’s content, rules, and capabilities up to date.

news.title: U.S. Voters Reject Dozens of AI Data Centers
news.description: During the midterm elections, U.S. voters approved 33 measures limiting AI data center projects, while six others were leading. The measures range from permanent bans to moratoriums and power limits.

news.title: Nvidia Will Be Able to Fulfill Only 1% of Chinese GPU Orders
news.description: Over the coming months, Nvidia will deliver only about 1% of the RTX Pro 5500 GPUs ordered by Chinese companies such as ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. Demand reportedly amounts to about $70 billion, far exceeding current production capacity.

news.title: Google Expands Voluntary Buyouts to Reduce Its Workforce
news.description: Google is expanding its voluntary departure programs to reduce its workforce without carrying out layoffs.

news.title: Apple Explicitly Bans the Use of Confidential Information in Prediction Markets
news.description: Apple now explicitly prohibits employees from using confidential information in prediction markets.

news.title: Neuralink’s Chinese Rival Targets Obesity with an Electronic GLP-1
news.description: Neuralink’s Chinese rival is seeking to treat obesity with an electronic GLP-1 treatment.

news.title: Microsoft Reveals Its Plan to Avoid a Windows 11 RAM Crisis
news.description: Microsoft is preparing a plan intended to avoid Windows 11 RAM problems.

news.title: The SaaS Apocalypse Began in October
news.description: The article claims that the software-as-a-service apocalypse began in October.

news.title: Oracle Abandons $7 Billion Deal with Tencent
news.description: Oracle is abandoning a $7 billion deal with Tencent under pressure from the Trump administration.

news.title: AI medical assistants sometimes access unnecessary identifiers
news.description: AI medical assistants sometimes access patient identifiers they do not need. Checking permissions before the task nearly eliminated these unnecessary accesses.

news.title: Gender influences AI’s automated candidate evaluations
news.description: A study shows that simply indicating a candidate’s gender changes approval rates by up to 1.7 points and reverses up to 3.3% of decisions.

news.title: Trust in national news media rises in the United States
news.description: American adults’ trust in national news media rose by six points in one year, to 62%. Trust in social media news remained stable at 38%, according to a Pew survey.

news.title: What an AI agent actually does
news.description: The chapter explains the difference between an AI that responds and one that acts, as well as the reliability of multistep tasks. It also shows which actions an agent can perform alone and which require human approval.

news.title: Connecting AI to the tools you already use
news.description: The chapter explains what connecting AI to a tool enables compared with sending files case by case. It helps identify the risks, protection settings and first system to connect.

news.title: Elon Musk’s failure in Texas despite his campaign spending
news.description: Elon Musk, the biggest donor in the 2026 midterm elections, gave at least 446 million dollars, about half of it in Texas. The state nevertheless shifted to the Democratic camp.

news.title: Texas turns Democratic, to the dismay of tech entrepreneurs
news.description: Texas shifted to the Democratic camp, disappointing entrepreneurs in the technology sector.

news.title: A Cybercab spotted near Florida Mall
news.description: A forum member says they found a Cybercab where route 417 meets World Drive, near Disney World. They list the next stops on its route, including a Marriott, I-4 and Disney World.

news.title: A Tesla’s tire pressure system stops working
news.description: A member reports that tire pressure is no longer displayed. A response explains that in the United States, regulations require a tire-pressure monitoring system, but not necessarily sensors, and that software monitoring of wheel behavior may be sufficient.

news.title: Trading Tesla referral codes for free FSD access
news.description: The discussion concerns the terms of use for Tesla referral codes, including a possible limit of 12 referrals per calendar year and the 48-month period mentioned by some members.

news.title: A Tesla owner considers a Rivian R2 for someone close to him
news.description: A close friend approaching retirement has long appreciated efficient electric vehicles but has never bought one. He is familiar with the member’s Teslas but has not yet taken the plunge.

news.title: Is the FSD price prorated mid-month?
news.description: A member asks how much a mid-month FSD subscription would cost for an upcoming trip, after a previous subscription expired.

news.title: Rear-impact repair estimated at nearly 4,000 dollars
news.description: Tesla and the insurance adjuster both estimated the repair at just under 4,000 dollars. The proposed solution is to straighten the dent, which does not fully convince the owner.

news.title: A Tesla’s windshield wipers skip across the glass
news.description: A member says they have not experienced this problem but believes it could come from the entire wiper arm assembly, which may be defective or have another fault.

news.title: At Orbia, employees present their own ideas to the CEO
news.description: At Orbia, the innovation team stays in the background so that employees who originated the ideas can present the results themselves and receive the credit. This rule contributes to a 75% engagement rate, compared with about 30% on average.

news.title: An innovation culture built by 1.25 people at the NHS
news.description: At Clatterbridge Cancer Centre, two people representing a combined 1.25 full-time equivalents created a system for collecting staff ideas and acting quickly. Their approach includes a dedicated ideas space, 30-minute “Time to Think” sessions and an accelerated governance pathway.

news.title: RBI rethinks its innovation program despite a 9.3 out of 10 rating
news.description: Raiffeisen Bank International’s Innovation School was viewed very positively by 92% of participants, but only 41% felt six months later that they had achieved their learning goal. The team applied design thinking to its own program and made four changes as a result.

news.title: Why most employees think innovation is not their job
news.description: Linda Hill of Harvard Business School explains that presenting innovation as an activity reserved for technologists alienates other employees. She suggests defining innovation as any useful novelty and connecting everyone’s daily work to the company’s mission.

news.title: Captain Picard’s final leadership lesson
news.description: While watching the final scene of Star Trek: The Next Generation, Bob Gilbreath rediscovers a leadership lesson: do not wait until the end to appreciate and support team members. Leaders must be authentic and present with their employees.

news.title: Snowflake unveils AI agents that work after you disconnect
news.description: Snowflake announced CoCo and CoWork Bots, agents under development that can handle tasks in the background and ask a human for help when needed. Recurring automations and planned integrations with Slack, spreadsheets and mobile devices were also announced.

news.title: Does AI save time or make work take longer?
news.description: The latest ActivTrak research links intensive AI use to longer workdays, shorter focus periods and more app switching. Differences between the samples and measurement limitations make the results difficult to compare.

news.title: Hasty AI-related layoffs could make rehiring costly
news.description: Gartner predicts that 30% of employees replaced by AI will be rehired by 2029, probably at a higher cost. The firm recommends assessing how work is changing before deciding which positions to eliminate.

news.title: Snowflake centralizes controls for enterprise AI agents
news.description: Snowflake’s Cortex AI Gateway, now available, centralizes policies governing agent connections, model access and spending. Business Ontology will let agents use approved definitions of business concepts, while sandbox execution and abuse detection remain in private preview.

news.title: Bull and Schwarz Digits plan sovereign European AI infrastructure
news.description: Bull and Schwarz Digits have signed an agreement to develop AI infrastructure for European organizations in regulated and strategic sectors. The planned architecture combines European cloud STACKIT with Bull’s computing hardware, liquid cooling and AI software.

news.title: National Grid plans major substation for data center expansion
news.description: National Grid plans a major substation in Teesside to supply a data center, battery storage and other electricity-intensive industries. Its initial capacity of 1,440 MVA is due to come online by the end of 2029.

news.title: CIO survey reveals gap between AI deployment and readiness
news.description: An Accenture survey of 300 technology leaders finds that 64% are accelerating enterprise AI deployment, but only 7% are optimizing it at scale. Adoption and user training are the main obstacles, and nearly half of companies still require manual approvals for IT operations agents.

news.title: UK businesses near deadline for migration to digital telephony
news.description: Openreach says about 300,000 copper business lines remain active ahead of the January deadline. They include connections used by payment terminals, alarms and building systems.

news.title: AI agents expected to drive a 55% increase in identity spending
news.description: Juniper Research forecasts that global spending on identity and access management will rise from 26.2 billion dollars in 2026 to 40.5 billion in 2031. The increase is driven by the growing number of AI agents and other nonhuman identities.

news.title: Responsibility for AI agents is still missing from organizational charts
news.description: A Gravitee survey finds that 85% of executives are under pressure to deploy more agents, while about 80% are concerned about their security and only 7% have appointed responsible owners. According to Rory Blundell, the challenge is more about governance and organizational accountability than technology itself.

news.title: Steve Aoki launches Archon, a video model that automates editing
news.description: Startup Selendis, founded by DJ Steve Aoki and industry experts, introduced Archon, a video model that turns raw footage into finished edits. The tool reportedly learns the user’s editing style, and its early access now has an open waitlist.

news.title: Seedance 2.5 lets you create impossible stunt videos with your own face
news.description: The tutorial explains how to use Higgsfield and Seedance 2.5 to generate a stunt video by providing two to five reference photos and, optionally, a video clip. It recommends checking facial consistency, movement and framing before generating the final version.

news.title: Smaller models can outperform frontier models at lower cost
news.description: Research cited in the newsletter shows that increasing reasoning effort can fail on some tasks while costing up to 42 times more. Several companies get better results by tuning small models to their needs and evaluating them with internal tests.

news.title: BrainCo is developing a brain device for obesity
news.description: Chinese company BrainCo is developing a wearable device that would reduce appetite by stimulating the brain. It aims to commercialize it in China within the next two to three years, before potentially expanding to the United States.

news.title: Longevity moves from biohacking into mainstream culture
news.description: The movement of biohackers and people taking greater control of their longevity became more mainstream with the COVID-19 pandemic and AI chatbots. Companies that help individuals take action and manage their health over time could benefit from the sector’s biggest opportunities.

news.title: AI speeds up software development but creates new constraints
news.description: AI-native startups can ship even faster than pre-AI startups, at the cost of a higher risk of breakage. New constraints include context switching, loss of shared context, pace, design and the limits of AI plans.

news.title: Interpolative software is easy to produce with AI models
news.description: Interpolative software exists in models’ training distribution and can often be specified in a few sentences. Novel software that has never existed before remains difficult to create with agents, even though most software is not novel.

news.title: The angel investor business model is deteriorating
news.description: Angel investing has become less attractive, with some investors finding it more profitable to create a fund. Startups move faster, and angel investors are often squeezed out by valuations.

news.title: SaaS company growth reversed in October
news.description: The median SaaS company’s revenue grew by 0.20% in September before falling by 0.41% the following month.

news.title: Namespace deploys Macs at scale for macOS and Xcode
news.description: Namespace is showcasing custom Mac rack construction, macOS instances that boot in seconds and new Xcode versions made available within hours of Apple’s release.

news.title: The true cost of tokens may be lower than the prices charged
news.description: The cost of operating servers appears to be significantly lower than the prices providers charge when their capacity is heavily utilized.

news.title: Safari adapts light websites to offer a dark mode
news.description: Safari’s adaptive dark mode transforms websites designed in light mode to display them in dark mode.

news.title: How software jobs have evolved since the 1940s
news.description: This article traces the evolution of job titles in software, from the 1940s to today.

news.title: Tech leaders react badly to Democratic victory
news.description: Texas has turned Democratic, disappointing several tech entrepreneurs. The election result sparked strong reactions among the “tech bros.”

news.title: Cost of living weighed on US midterm elections
news.description: High prices and the cost of living helped shape the US midterm elections.

news.title: Trump says voters support Iran policy, but not gas prices
news.description: Donald Trump says voters can support his Iran policy while rejecting the amount of their gas bills.

news.title: Democratic control reshuffles the deck in Washington
news.description: The election result upends the balance of power in Washington, creating winners and losers in the business world.

news.title: DEI’s return becomes a meme after Democratic victory
news.description: Online, diversity, equity, and inclusion appear to be returning as a meme rather than as policy. Some are wondering whether workplace policy will change.

news.title: Boulder authorizes Airbnb rentals for four weeks during Sundance
news.description: Boulder is temporarily lifting its ban on most short-term rentals so residents can rent out their homes for four weeks in January and February. The measure accompanies the arrival of the Sundance Film Festival, while the city expects about 100,000 visitors but has only 3,000 hotel rooms.

news.title: Gold is down 29% from its January peak
news.description: The precious metal has fallen about 29% from its January high. Analysts explain the causes of this unusual decline as stocks are also falling.

news.title: Investment chief recommends eight AI-related stocks
news.description: David Katz, chief investment officer at Matrix Asset Advisers, believes the sell-off in AI-related stocks is over. He sees the decline as a buying opportunity and shared eight stocks he would buy.

news.title: Ken Griffin’s Citadel fund gains 1.7% in October
news.description: Most major managers lost money in October, which included one of the worst days for hedge funds since the pandemic. Ken Griffin’s Citadel fund, however, gained 1.7%.

news.title: Couple killed in Learjet crash in Florida
news.description: Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr met at a hostel in Peru in 2019 before falling in love and opening a boutique hotel in Honduras. They died Sunday in a plane crash in Florida.

news.title: Cava CEO describes a day centered on Mediterranean cuisine
news.description: Brett Schulman has led the Mediterranean restaurant chain Cava for 15 years. He shared a typical day, from latte art to a daily Cava bowl.

news.title: Chipotle’s chief operating officer shares four leadership tips
news.description: Jason Kidd, Chipotle’s chief operating officer, visits about twelve restaurants a week. He explains the four qualities he looks for in employees who may be promoted.

news.title: New York City Marathon runner dies at 24
news.description: A New York City Marathon runner died suddenly at age 24. Her family attributes her death to rhabdomyolysis, a rare risk even among fit athletes.

news.title: Students launch legal startup during exam week
news.description: Students created a legal technology startup during their exam week. Their business now takes priority over their studies.

news.title: Photos from the 2026 New York City Marathon capture race highlights
news.description: A selection of photos revisits the 2026 New York City Marathon, from celebrity appearances to record-setting finishes.

news.title: Bill Ackman expects hyperscaler revenue to beat forecasts
news.description: Bill Ackman believes AI hyperscalers’ revenue will far exceed forecasts, despite growing concerns about their capital spending.

news.title: Anthropic aims to double computing capacity to 7 GW
news.description: Anthropic plans to increase its computing capacity from 3.5 GW to about 7 GW next year. According to the New York Times, that electricity consumption would equal that of all Chicago households.

news.title: Apple warns its AI agents could act without authorization
news.description: In its annual report, Apple says AI agents could act unintentionally or unpredictably, including by carrying out transactions without the proper authorizations.

news.title: EU court adviser says chatbots can violate publishers’ rights
news.description: An adviser to the European Union’s highest court says chatbots can infringe publishers’ rights by reusing copyrighted content. The opinion concerns a case involving Google Gemini and is nonbinding.

news.title: Laid-off workers in AI-exposed sectors take longer to find jobs
news.description: Goldman Sachs found that workers likely to be replaced by AI in 2025 took about one month longer to find a new job than other laid-off employees.

news.title: CrowdStrike launches kill switch for unauthorized AI agents
news.description: CrowdStrike’s feature stops an unauthorized AI agent in real time and prevents it from operating again within the organization. Endpoint deployment is planned for later.

news.title: Anthropic experiment shows analysts follow an AI’s random preferences
news.description: Anthropic randomly assigned an agent a preference between two defensible options and then observed 50 analysts. They followed their agent’s preference in 86% of the decisions studied.

news.title: Claude responds 35% faster in very long conversations
news.description: Anthropic is rolling out Message Threads in public beta. The feature cuts the time to the first token by about 35% for requests of 500,000 to 1 million tokens, without reducing token usage.

news.title: Google satellite sends an AI-written haiku from orbit
news.description: The prototype satellite Project Suncatcher received a prompt while flying over Svalbard, then Gemma 4 composed a haiku about space. Google plans to test the chips’ resilience before launching two interconnected satellites in 2027.

news.title: Colibrì runs a 744-billion-parameter model with 25 GB of RAM
news.description: This engine written entirely in C runs the Chinese GLM-5.2 model on consumer hardware. Only about 40 billion parameters are active for each generated word, and the model core fits in about 9.9 GB of RAM.

news.title: 44% of highly cited LLM claims are already outdated
news.description: Stanford researchers tested 50 claims across 20 current models: 44% no longer hold, and 34% have substantially lost validity. Their average lifespan is 15.7 months.

news.title: Google DeepMind adds chemistry skills to Antigravity
news.description: In an example involving lung cancer treatments, an agent examined thousands of compounds and proposed new molecules with their synthesis routes in about an hour. Deterministic tools such as RDKit are used to limit errors.

news.title: IBM introduces Palette, a small open model for creating presentations
news.description: This open 20-billion-parameter model can be self-hosted and generates presentations according to a visual identity. A designer role plans the slides, and a coder role produces them.

news.title: StateBench highlights large models’ difficulties with long documents
news.description: The Allen AI benchmark evaluates models’ ability to track changes in a text. Several large models falter on difficult cases as documents grow longer, while recurrent and hybrid models generalize better.

news.title: An “inverse game theory” approach to better control AI agents
news.description: This approach seeks to design rules that encourage models to behave well rather than examine their internal workings. It has attracted interest after several cases of models concealing their intentions or deceiving evaluators.

news.title: Kairos offers an open-source antifraud tool controllable by AI agents
news.description: Finic is launching an open-source alternative to Sift and Sardine for assessing fraud risk in real time. An MCP server allows Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex to create decision workflows and train models.

news.title: Images showing Jeff Bezos with hair are fake
news.description: Images showing Jeff Bezos and Jason Statham with full heads of hair are circulating across several social networks. The Verge confirms they are composites but cannot determine whether AI was used to create them.

news.title: Google will disable its AI by default for students
news.description: Gemini, NotebookLM, and Gemini in Classroom will be disabled by default for students unless administrators enable them. Schools that completely block AI will also lose Google Search, while Google is launching Guided Learning.

news.title: Sonos opens voice assistant early access on November 6
news.description: Sonos 27voice understands natural language, controls playback and compatible devices, sets timers, and answers general questions. Access is limited to the United States and English, subject to approval.

news.title: Nvidia asks cloud providers to reduce business with China
news.description: Nvidia reportedly verbally asked some providers to take on fewer Chinese customers and identify who is actually using its chips. The nonmandatory guidance notably targets remote access to chips from data centers located abroad.

news.title: European adviser says Gemini responses could be illegal
news.description: A headline published by AI Secret claims that Gemini’s responses could constitute an offense. Because the accessible content is limited to a sign-up form, the nature of the offense and the adviser’s identity cannot be verified.

news.title: Texas’s political shift could disrupt AI data centers
news.description: The election of Democrats as governor and to the US Senate could create uncertainty for Texas’s AI data center sector. The concrete consequences for the industry and Elon Musk remain unclear.

news.title: Palantir sharply increases revenue but shortens its contracts
news.description: Palantir’s revenue reached 2.31 billion dollars, up 96% year over year. However, the value of contracts signed with US companies fell from 2.13 to 1.46 billion dollars in one quarter.

news.title: AMD expects a sharp acceleration in revenue thanks to AI
news.description: AMD expects its revenue to rise by around 66% year over year in the current quarter, followed by growth of more than 80% next year. These forecasts reflect continued strong demand for AI hardware.

news.title: Hidden AI-related commitments reach $3.2 trillion
news.description: According to Nikkei Asia, AI-related commitments that major US tech companies do not carry directly on their balance sheets amount to around $3.2 trillion. This situation is increasingly worrying investors, particularly because of spending on data centers.

news.title: Wall Street remains divided over a potential AI bubble burst
news.description: Wall Street players disagree on the risks associated with AI, and no one can predict when a potential burst might occur. Doubts about the sector’s financial strength persist among major fund managers.
